## Setting
Choice of a campus facility improvement plan for the coming fiscal year. A five-member university committee of faculty and administrative staff reviews the facility plans submitted by departments. One plan will be carried out with next year's capital budget. Participants: Benjamin, Shizue, Mizuki, Yumi and George. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Tender records over three budget cycles
- Renewal reserve for equipment bought earlier
- Survey findings in the older blocks
- Weather days in the site diaries
- Decade of delivery schedules by project rationale
- Post-occupancy review ratings
- Timetable records on rooms out of service
- Booking data for specialist and general rooms
- Staffing posts since the hiring freeze
- Bench technicians' weekly manual routines

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Shizue, Yumi, George, Mizuki and Benjamin. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. ## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the candidates | 4 turns | every participant votes; the candidate with the most votes is selected |

If votes are tied, one of the tied candidates is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

## Participants
Name: Benjamin
Age: 28
Gender: male
Personality: Benjamin is an intelligent and calm person. He is able to think calmly and rationally, and even in emotional situations, he places importance on logic. In public, he is elegant and polite, often incorporating sarcasm and humor into his conversations, but he is skilled at doing so without hurting others, creating a harmonious atmosphere. He also has an introverted side, often engrossed in deep thought, and occasionally keeps his distance from those around him. However, his calmness and knowledge are factors that earn him the trust of others even in difficult situations.
Concern: The figures approved on paper no longer survive contact with the market, and what a building costs after it opens never reaches the committee at all.

Name: Shizue
Age: 78
Gender: female
Personality: Shizue has a very calm and gentle personality. Even as she has grown older, she continues to smile warmly at those around her and is a very caring person. She is always considerate of others, friendly, and sometimes shows a playful side. She often reaches out to those who are feeling down with kind words and never hesitates to lend a helping hand when needed, which has earned her the affection of many people in the village and community. Through her years of life experience, Shizue has come to understand the importance of living peacefully with others.
Concern: Every recent job seems to meet something nobody priced for, and the calendar keeps slipping until a year of building is squeezed into whatever weeks are left.

Name: Mizuki
Age: 24
Gender: female
Personality: Mizuki is a very confident woman who is often relied upon by those around her. She is calm and logical in her thinking and is good at observing people. As a result, she always makes calm judgments and chooses her actions according to the situation around her. Although she may sometimes come across as a little aloof, she is actually very caring and cannot ignore those who are weak. While she is relied upon by those around her and occasionally asserts her opinions strongly, she also possesses a kindness that considers others.
Concern: Looking back at what has actually been built here, nobody has asked in the open which of those projects landed well and which quietly disappointed the people using them.

Name: Yumi
Age: 16
Gender: female
Personality: Yumi has a cheerful and energetic personality. She is modest, yet she also has a kind side that cares about those around her. She has a calm personality, but she is very passionate toward her friends and family, and she cannot ignore people in trouble. She smiles at the slightest thing and spreads positive energy to those around her. She is friendly and can quickly get along with people she meets for the first time.
Concern: Some of us keep noticing that space decisions are settled without asking what the timetable absorbs while the work runs, or how heavily the finished rooms get used afterwards.

Name: George
Age: 65
Gender: male
Personality: George has a gentle and calm personality, but he can also be a little stubborn and headstrong at times. He is seen by those around him as a reliable person with a wealth of experience appropriate for his age, and he is always able to make calm judgments, allowing him to handle difficult situations without panicking. However, his expressions sometimes reveal a hint of sternness or awkwardness, and he tends to observe things from a step back rather than actively engaging with others. He is very independent and tends to try to solve problems on his own without relying on others.
Concern: Each decision here lands on the same shrinking set of staff, and those already carrying the routine upkeep have had no relief for years.

## Hidden information
The candidates and the full text of every card are listed here. The participants do not know them before the schedule above says so, and nothing from them may appear in the talk before the round in which it is revealed.

Candidates (see the schedule above):
- A: Campus Path Network. A reworking of the walkways between the main buildings, covering lighting, surface renewal, sheltered sections, and wayfinding signage for visitors and new students.
- B: Media Production Center. A fitted-out suite of recording and editing rooms for course video, student projects, and public lectures, managed through a booking system open to campus users.
- C: Central Study Commons. A conversion of an underused ground-floor hall into open study space, with bookable group rooms, distributed power outlets, and a service desk near the entrance.
- D: Laboratory Ventilation Upgrade. A replacement of ventilation and fume extraction equipment throughout the shared teaching laboratories, together with revised layouts for the bench, storage, and preparation areas.

Cards (see the schedule above; title: text):
- Tender records over three budget cycles: Tender records over three budget cycles show mechanical and ducted plant lots rising by about a fifth, while surfacing and lamp-column lots held near the index.
- Renewal reserve for equipment bought earlier: Audiovisual kit bought in an earlier capital round is written down over five years, yet no renewal reserve was ever opened to pay for replacing it.
- Survey findings in the older blocks: Surveys in the older blocks keep finding hazardous material behind ground-floor partitions, and the last two openings there added months before any contractor could begin.
- Weather days in the site diaries: Site diaries from the last two capital jobs record six working weeks lost to rain and frost, all of it on work exposed to the weather.
- Decade of delivery schedules by project rationale: Over the last decade, works answering an inspection finding were delivered on schedule, while those argued for on comfort or enrolment appeal slipped a year or more.
- Post-occupancy review ratings: Post-occupancy reviews rated finished work highest where any department could book the space afterwards, and lowest where the benefit stayed inside a single wing.
- Timetable records on rooms out of service: Timetable records show every room taken out of service for works has to be replaced by hired space off site, which the division paid for over two terms.
- Booking data for specialist and general rooms: Booking data from the specialist rooms shows them idle outside a few weeks each term, while requests for general-purpose rooms are turned away all year.
- Staffing posts since the hiring freeze: Since the hiring freeze, front-of-house and grounds posts have stayed unfilled, while the technicians taken on during the online teaching push still have hours to spare.
- Bench technicians' weekly manual routines: Bench technicians log several hours each week on manual checks and window-opening routines that the current extraction equipment cannot carry out by itself.

## Round 1
### Talk
#### Turn 1 of 4
- **Shizue**: I’d like to start by asking: which of the listed records might show us where our timelines have quietly slipped in recent years?
- **Yumi**: @Shizue, the weather days in the site diaries seem like the best place to start for that.
- **George**: @Yumi, that’s a fair point, but I’d also look at the decade of delivery schedules to see if the slippage is consistent across different project types.
- **Mizuki**: @George, I agree. I’d also check the post-occupancy review ratings to see if the delays actually hurt the people using the spaces.
- **Benjamin**:

response: @Mizuki, I’d also check the tender records to see if the budget figures we approved actually match what the market is charging now.
